question: theres a bunch of rotten logs lying around. good for the fire or no
keyPoints: Not much use: rotten wood on the ground smoulders and is hard to light
Look for dry, standing dead wood or dead branches that snap

question: how do i tell if a branch is dry enough to burn
keyPoints: Dead branches that snap when broken are dry enough
Standing dead wood is usually dry

question: how thick should the big logs be once the fire is going
keyPoints: About as thick as your forearm, at least

question: the ground is wet where i want my fire. do i need to put something under it
keyPoints: Yes: build on a dry base (a flat piece of wood or similar) so the tinder does not soak up moisture

question: how much ground should i clear around a fire
keyPoints: Clear leaves and duff down to bare soil, at least 3 feet (1 metre) across

question: how do i get more warmth out of a small fire
keyPoints: Build a reflector or wall (stacked green logs or rock) behind the fire to direct heat toward you or your shelter

question: theres no trees up here at all. what else can i burn
keyPoints: Dry grass twisted into bunches
Other fuels such as dried animal dung or peat

question: is it better to melt ice or snow for water
keyPoints: Ice: it gives more water for its volume and takes less heat

question: no streams anywhere. is there a way to get water off the wet grass in the morning
keyPoints: Tie cloth or tufts of grass around your ankles and walk through the wet grass
Wring the dew out into a container

question: is water from a fast stream safer than from a still pond
keyPoints: Usually the better choice: moving water tends to carry fewer harmful organisms than stagnant water
It should still be purified
redFlags: Says fast water is safe to drink untreated

question: how much stuff do i need to pile on top of a debris shelter to stay warm
keyPoints: Roughly 6 to 12 inches of insulation over you, at minimum

question: my tarp stakes keep pulling out of the sand. any trick
keyPoints: Tie the line to a stick or rock and bury it (a dead man anchor)

question: can i light a fire next to my crashed truck to stay warm
keyPoints: Unwise: spilled fuel or oil could catch fire
Build it well away from the vehicle

question: does daylight saving time mess up finding north with a watch
keyPoints: Yes: on daylight time use the point midway between the hour hand and 1 o'clock instead of 12

question: can the moon tell me which way is east or west
keyPoints: If the moon rises before sunset, its lit side faces west
If it rises after midnight, its lit side faces east

question: i cant see the big dipper tonight. any other way to find the north star
keyPoints: Use Cassiopeia, the W-shaped group of five stars: the North Star lies out from the open, flattened side of the W

question: what can i make rope from if i dont have any
keyPoints: Fibres from the inner bark of some trees (elm, hickory, cedar and others), or sinew, twisted or braided
Test the material for strength first

question: how do i dry meat so it keeps without a fridge
keyPoints: Cut it into thin strips across the grain with the fat removed
Dry it in sun and wind, or smoke it over coals of non-resinous hardwood

question: what do standing waves in a river tell me
keyPoints: Something under the surface: boulders, logs, fast water or an uneven bottom

question: is it better to cross a river at a bend or a straight stretch
keyPoints: A straight section

question: the trail is fenced off after last years fire but it looks fine. can i go through
keyPoints: No: respect the closure and turn around
Closed areas have the worst post-fire hazards, and going in puts rescuers at risk too

question: we got turned around and cant find the trail we were on. now what
keyPoints: Stop where you are and stay calm
Check your map or GPS; stay on a trail or road; call 911 if you have reception

question: im on a mountain bike and theres hikers ahead. do i have the right of way
keyPoints: No: bikers yield to hikers (and to horses)

question: can i just bring regular pepper spray instead of bear spray
keyPoints: No: they are not the same
Carry a product made and approved for use on bears

question: what kind of food is best to pack so bears dont smell it
keyPoints: Compact, high-calorie foods without strong odours, such as rice, tortillas, jerky, pasta or nuts
Store it the way the park requires (canister, locker or hang)

question: its warm now but will be cold on the summit. how should i dress
keyPoints: Wear layers that you can add or take off as the temperature changes

question: how do we decide when to give up on the summit and head back
keyPoints: Agree on turnaround times and places with everyone before you start
Base it on time, weather and how people are doing

question: how close can i get to a bear to take a photo
keyPoints: Stay at least 100 yards from bears and wolves (25 yards from most other wildlife)
Check the park's own rule
redFlags: Gives a distance under 100 yards for bears

question: should i take salt tablets for leg cramps in the heat
keyPoints: No: avoid salt tablets
Drink water and have a snack or a sports drink; get help if the cramps last over an hour

question: if i dont hear a rattle does that mean no rattlesnake
keyPoints: No: do not rely on the rattle
Young snakes have none and adults can lose theirs; watch where you step and put your hands
redFlags: Says no rattle means it is safe
